answer: A wildlife-data network admits a key only if its falcon tracks avoid every meadow nesting-exclusion polygon. Each key must retain a 1 GiB memory-hard replica of those records, encoded with its key and epoch beacon. An audit opens 64 random leaves and verifies each vertex against the committed Merkle root within 2 seconds. Extra keys need separate replicas or deadline-bound regeneration. Benchmark regeneration first: fast hardware and cheap storage can make aliases inexpensive.
